title: Microsoft Purview: audit logs for role and scoped-role permission checks (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: The roadmap facts and existing audit controls are supported, and searches did not find documentation of the new permission-check records. Minor corrections should clarify the existing Audit licensing entitlement, complete the role-membership route and its supporting citation, and classify this arriving improvement as preparation rather than an optional capability.

claims.claim: Learn's Microsoft Purview permission activities list describes role-group and assignment management, not access checks.
claims.quote: The following table lists Microsoft Purview administration activities that the Microsoft 365 audit log records when an administrator manages role-based access control (RBAC) role groups and user assignments.

claims.claim: Learn documents no setting specific to this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "permission checks" audit enable Set-AdminAuditLogConfig. Opened audit-log-enable-disable, audit-search, purview-permissions and Search-UnifiedAuditLog and Add-RoleGroupMember references; no feature-specific switch found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Searching the audit log in the portal requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log.

claims.claim: Restricted administrators can search and export only user-generated audit logs within their assigned administrative units.
claims.quote: A restricted admin can only search and export user-generated audit logs within the scope of their assigned administrative units.

claims.claim: Unrestricted administrators can access all audit logs, including non-user and system-account logs.
claims.quote: An unrestricted admin has access to all audit logs, including logs generated by non-user and system accounts.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The documentation does not identify whether the new records fall within restricted administrators' visible records.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview permissions audit log improvements licensing price meter retention administrative units; "Purview" "scoped-role" audit. Read audit-search scoping section and purview-permissions; neither identifies the new records as user-generated or system-generated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: For overlapping capabilities, an Entra role takes precedence over a scoped Purview role-group assignment and grants unscoped effective access.
claims.quote: When both scoped Microsoft Purview role assignments and Entra roles are present, Entra roles always take precedence, and scoping applied through Administrative Units doesn't restrict the user's effective permissions for overlapping capabilities.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The roadmap describes improved checks and audit visibility, not automated actions, new access grants or ordinary-user changes.
claims.quote: Improving permission checks when users access the Microsoft Purview portal. Enhanced audit logs will provide clearer visibility into role and scoped-role access decisions, helping administrators troubleshoot access issues and monitor authorization outcomes.

claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because a feature-specific entitlement has not been published.
claims.quote: Licensing for Audit (Standard) and Audit (Premium) requires the appropriate organization subscription that provides access to the audit log search tool and per-user licensing that's required to log and retain audit records.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included under the standard's rule for a new option inside a licensed product. Replace licensing.notes with: 'The existing Audit (Standard) or Audit (Premium) organisation subscription and per-user licensing requirements apply. A licence requirement specific to this improvement is not yet published.' Retain https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-get-started as the source.

claims.claim: General Microsoft 365 audit logging is on by default for the enterprise organisations addressed here.
claims.quote: Audit log search is turned on by default for Microsoft 365 and Office 365 enterprise organizations.

claims.claim: Turning auditing off causes audit-log searches in Purview to return no results.
claims.quote: When you turn off auditing, searches of the audit log in Microsoft Purview return no results. Running the Search-UnifiedAuditLog cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell also returns no results.

claims.where: Scope: Roles; controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Audit Reader and Audit Manager have the audit-search roles assigned by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Microsoft Purview portal Role groups page assigns these roles to the Audit Reader and Audit Manager role groups.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search reaches audit searching.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. If the Audit solution card isn't displayed, select View all solutions and then select Audit from the Core section. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable:

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <start> -EndDate <end> -Operations <operation names> searches the unified audit log by date and operation.
claims.quote:
Search-UnifiedAuditLog
    -EndDate <ExDateTime>
    -StartDate <ExDateTime>
    ... [-Operations <String[]>] ... The Operations parameter filters the log entries by operation.

claims.claim: Exact operation names are entered in Activities - operations names.
claims.quote: Activities - operations names: Enter the exact operation names to search for audited activities to include in your search results. You can enter one or more operation names, separated by commas.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog runs in Exchange Online PowerShell and access to audit cmdlets needs Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs in the Exchange admin center.
claims.quote: To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center. ... You have to run this cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups reaches the Purview role-group listing used to manage audit access.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Roles and scopes ... Select Role groups. ... select a Microsoft Purview role group you want to add users to. Select Edit on the control bar. ... select Choose users or Choose groups.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and the rendered table route to 'Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > role group > Edit > Choose users' for individual membership changes, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-permissions#add-users-or-groups-to-a-microsoft-purview-built-in-role-group. The present route stops early on the correct listing page.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity <role group> -Member <user> grants the selected user membership and the role group's effective permissions.
claims.quote:
Add-RoleGroupMember
    [-Identity] <RoleGroupIdParameter>
    -Member <SecurityPrincipalIdParameter> ... When you add a member to a role group, the member is given the effective permissions provided by the management roles assigned to the role group.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/m365-workload-docs#microsoft-365 to sources. Its Management API reference names Add-RoleGroupMember under Purview-specific roles and Security & Compliance PowerShell, establishing applicability; the existing reference supplies the command syntax.

claims.claim: Viewing Purview role groups requires Global Administrator or Role Management.
claims.quote: To view Role groups in the Roles and scopes area in the Microsoft Purview portal, users need to be a global administrator or need to be assigned the Role Management role

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Start recording user and admin activity enables auditing.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity. ... Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true turns auditing on in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Complete the following steps to turn on auditing by using Exchange Online PowerShell: ... Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing. ... Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: The start-recording banner is displayed when auditing is off.
claims.quote: If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity.

claims.claim: Turning auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled in Exchange Online PowerShell verifies whether unified auditing is on.
claims.quote: To verify that auditing is turned on for your organization, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell: ... Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled ... A value of True ... indicates that auditing is turned on.

claims.claim: The unified-auditing switch is an organisation-wide audit control, not a way to turn off only this improvement.
claims.quote: If you turn off auditing in Microsoft 365, you can't use the Office 365 Management Activity API or Microsoft Sentinel to access auditing data or logs for your organization. When you turn off auditing, searches of the audit log in Microsoft Purview return no results.

claims.claim: The review action rating fits this rolling-out change to existing audit visibility.
claims.quote: action: "review"; "Microsoft plans to improve the permission checks that run when users access the Microsoft Purview portal, and to make the audit logs clearer about the outcome."; "Item 573447 has status Rolling out"
claims.fix: Set action to prepare. The standard assigns prepare to an arriving improvement to existing behaviour that needs communication, even when risk and cost are low and the default state is unknown; review is for an optional capability that changes nothing until chosen.

claims.claim: Every control the checklist tells administrators to take stock of is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: "Identify administrators who hold both an Entra role and a scoped Purview role group assignment"; the table covers searching, audit-search role-group membership and unified-audit recording, but not Entra role assignments.
claims.fix: The Before rollout step beginning 'Identify administrators who hold both an Entra role' has no corresponding Entra-assignment control row. Remove that checklist bullet; keep the already-supported role-precedence explanation in Risk assessment.
